summary: Frontend-only iteration 5 testing of (a) /percorso vertical-timeline rewrite, (b) large faint watermark numbers on the 4 criterio pages, (c) content integrity of the Percorso refactor, and (d) full regression (6 nav routes, 5 inline deep-links, criterio TOC, tint bands, titles, footer, overflow at 1920/1280/390). Content integrity verified two ways: git-diff prose comparison (/app/tests/content_integrity_check.py => missing=[] for Percorso, Criterio.jsx prose SAME) and exact string comparison of all 4 stage paragraphs rendered in the browser vs. the pre-refactor HEAD text - all verbatim, nothing dropped or altered. Timeline renders correctly (1px navy/25% left border, 10px filled navy dots bg rgb(30,58,107) centered on the line at desktop and mobile, all 4 stage titles exact, all FadeIn opacity resolved to 1 after scroll). Watermark numbers verified on all 4 criterio pages (34 sections total): 96px desktop / 60px mobile, font-weight 100, color rgba(30,58,107,0.1), aria-hidden=true, z-index 0 vs H2 z-index 10 so titles stay fully legible. TOC still renders and click-scrolls (section lands at top=100px) and highlights on scroll. No console errors, no horizontal overflow anywhere. One real layout defect found: the intended 64px spacing between timeline stages is nullified.

ui_bugs.issue: Vertical spacing between timeline stages is 0px. The stage div uses 'pb-16 last:pb-0', but each stage div is the ONLY child of its <FadeIn> motion wrapper, so :last-child matches EVERY stage and pb-0 wins on all four. Measured computed padding-bottom = 0px on stages 1-4 and the gap between a stage's paragraph bottom and the next stage's H2 top = 0px / 0px / 0px. Result: each paragraph visually collides with the following title (very cramped, worse on mobile). Fix: put the spacing class on the FadeIn wrapper (e.g. <FadeIn className={i < stages.length - 1 ? 'pb-16' : ''}>) or use 'pb-16 [&:last-child]:pb-0' on the wrapper instead of the inner div.

issues: Watermark number is left-aligned at exactly the same left edge as the H2 (dxTitleVsWm = 0) and overlaps the title band by ~40-48px, so at desktop only the upper ~40% of the digits is visible - it reads as a clipped number rather than a full magazine watermark. Consider offsetting it further left (negative left) or further up so the whole numeral is visible behind/next to the title. Mobile (390) renders better since the number sits mostly above the title.

Opening paragraph now uses Body (18px) instead of the previous Lead (20/24px), so there is no visual hierarchy between H1 and the opening line. Flagging only in case this style downgrade was unintended by the timeline rewrite (text itself unchanged).

Clicking a TOC entry for a short section can leave aria-current on the NEXT entry (reproduced: /metriche-e-statuto toc-valuation-metriche -> active became toc-investitori-piccoli; /prima-che-manchi-la-liquidita toc-fatturato-cassa -> active toc-startup-valore). Cause: IntersectionObserver rootMargin '-45% 0px -50% 0px' leaves only a ~5%-tall detection band at mid-viewport, which short sections scrolled to top=100px never reach. Pre-existing behaviour, low severity; loosening the rootMargin (e.g. -30% / -55%) would fix it.

action_items: HIGH: Restore inter-stage spacing on /percorso - 'last:pb-0' matches every stage because each is wrapped in its own FadeIn; move pb-16 to the FadeIn wrapper.
LOW: Consider offsetting criterio watermark numbers (left/top) so the whole numeral is visible at desktop instead of being half-covered by the H2.
LOW: Optionally loosen criterio TOC IntersectionObserver rootMargin so short sections become active after a TOC click.
critical_code_review_comments: Percorso.jsx: Tailwind 'last:' variants are unreliable when each item is wrapped in an animation component - the variant resolves against the wrapper's children, not the list. Apply spacing on the wrapper element.
Criterio.jsx SectionHeading: watermark uses absolute left-0 with the same left origin as the H2; a small negative left/top would achieve the intended magazine effect without clipping.
No other issues: watermark correctly aria-hidden + pointer-events-none + select-none, z-index layering correct, no hardcoded URLs, static site so no API concerns.

success_rate.frontend: 96% (all functional/content checks pass; 1 layout defect + 2 minor design/UX notes)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Correct testids: /ai-senza-governance uses ai-page/ai-title (NOT ai-governance-*). Criterio sections expose [data-testid=section-<id>] and TOC buttons [data-testid=toc-<id>]; note the 'Dove sta il valore' section still has legacy id 'dove-sta-il-lavoro' on all 4 pages (title text is correct as 'Dove sta il valore'). 5 inline deep-links confirmed: 1 on /assetti-societari, 1 on /processi, 1 on /finanza, 2 on /. Tint band testids: home-in-evidenza, assetti-come-lavoro, processi-come-lavoro, finanza-come-lavoro. Percorso content verified verbatim against git HEAD. After the spacing fix, re-check gap between [data-testid=timeline-stage-N] p bottom and stage-N+1 h2 top (should be ~64px).
rca_of_the_issue: Percorso stage spacing: <FadeIn> renders a motion.div wrapper per stage, and the stage <div className='relative pb-16 last:pb-0'> is the sole child of that wrapper, so the CSS :last-child in Tailwind's 'last:' variant always matches and overrides pb-16 with padding-bottom:0. Confirmed in browser: computed paddingBottom '0px' and parentElement.lastElementChild === el for all 4 stages, producing 0px gaps between stages.
